cards.explanation: The answer is gods of silver or gold, friends. God says, “You are not to make any gods alongside Me; you are not to make for yourselves gods of silver or gold.” (Exodus 20:23) That comes right after He reminds them that He has spoken to them from heaven. People can shape silver and gold into something shiny, but it's still just metal that somebody made.

The answer is False. Sinai isn't the limit, friends. God says, “In every place where I cause My name to be remembered, I will come to you and bless you.” (Exodus 20:24) Wherever He causes His name to be remembered, He promises to come and bless. That's a promise bigger than any one mountain.

The answer is defile it, friends. God says, “for if you use a chisel on it, you will defile it.” (Exodus 20:25) So an altar of stones can't be built with stones shaped by tools. I love a sharp edge on a stamper, but God has His own rules for His altar, and I'm not touching those.

The reason is that the Israelites were foreigners in Egypt, and it's right there in the verse. God says, “You must not exploit or oppress a foreign resident, for you yourselves were foreigners in the land of Egypt.” (Exodus 22:21) The Israelites know what it's like to be the newcomer. God points them straight back to their own story.

The answer is True, friends. God says, “If you do mistreat them, and they cry out to Me in distress, I will surely hear their cry.” (Exodus 22:23) Widows and orphans are not forgotten by Him. The word is “surely.” It's a heavy passage, but this part is a comfort.

The word is interest, friends. God says the lender “…must not act as a creditor to him; you are not to charge him interest.” (Exodus 22:25) The man is poor, and he's one of God's people. So the loan comes without a charge on top.

The reason is that it's the neighbor's only covering, friends. God says, “…his cloak is the only covering he has for his body. What else will he sleep in?” (Exodus 22:27) It's his one blanket, so it goes home at sunset. If I had one apron and somebody kept it overnight, I'd be in a cold kitchen too.

The answer is False, friends. God says, “…do not show favoritism to a poor man in his lawsuit.” (Exodus 23:3) And He adds, “You shall not deny justice to the poor in their lawsuits.” (Exodus 23:6) Justice in the courtroom means fair for everybody.

The word is return, friends. God says, “…you must return it to him.” (Exodus 23:4) Even when it's your enemy's ox or donkey that has wandered off. I think walking an enemy's donkey home would feel like the longest walk of your week.

The answer is that a bribe blinds those who see, friends. God says, “Do not accept a bribe, for a bribe blinds those who see and twists the words of the righteous.” (Exodus 23:8) Two things named there: it blinds those who see, and it twists the words of the righteous. Somebody who sees the situation clearly takes the bribe, and suddenly they can't see it anymore. That's why God says to stay away from it.

The rest is so the poor can eat from it, friends. God says the land rests in the seventh year “…so that the poor among your people may eat from the field and the wild animals may consume what they leave.” (Exodus 23:11) The poor eat from the field, and the wild animals get what they leave. Six years of sowing, then a whole year where the field feeds others. I can't even rest my ovens for one afternoon.

The answer is True, friends, and the ox and donkey are named. God says, “…on the seventh day you must cease, so that your ox and your donkey may rest and the son of your maidservant may be refreshed, as well as the foreign resident.” (Exodus 23:12) The ox, the donkey, the son of the maidservant and the foreign resident are all in that list. Even the donkey, who I'm sure has opinions.

The answer is the names of other gods, friends. God says, “You must not invoke the names of other gods; they must not be heard on your lips.” (Exodus 23:13) He says it right after telling them to pay close attention to everything He's said. Don't even say their names.

The reason is that Israel left Egypt that month, friends. God says they eat unleavened bread for seven days in the month of Abib “…because that was the month you came out of Egypt.” (Exodus 23:15) The leaving is the reason He gives for that month. I can't even remember what I ate last Tuesday, and Israel gets a whole month with the day they walked out of Egypt attached to it.

The answer is False, friends. God says, “No one may appear before Me empty-handed.” (Exodus 23:15) The people come to the feast and they come with something in their hands. Showing up with nothing is out.

The answer is the best of it, friends. God says, “Bring the best of the firstfruits of your soil to the house of the LORD your God.” (Exodus 23:19) The best of the firstfruits is what goes to His house. When guests come to my bakery, the best cookies go on the front of the tray. The broken ones are for me, and I've made peace with that.
